deviation_assessment.replaced_if_val_positive_gate: approved — the `if val_ret > 0.0` gate was replaced with `(_cfg.PHASE2_JOINT_TRAIN_VAL or getattr(_cfg, 'PHASE2_VAL_IN_FITNESS_PENALTY', False))`. This is acceptable because: (1) in default config (PHASE2_JOINT_TRAIN_VAL=True), the penalty fires for ANY sign of val_ret, so the bug is fully fixed in practice; (2) the replacement gate is a meta-gate controlling whether val-derived penalties enter fitness at all, which is semantically correct — it preserves the existing C6 test contract (test_val_penalties_gated_closed) that asserts val penalties must not leak when both gates are closed; (3) removing the gate entirely would break the C6 test, which would be a larger, unjustified deviation; (4) the implementer was transparent about this in the handoff notes.
deviation_assessment.rationale: The plan's intent ('penalty well-defined for any sign of val_ret') is fully preserved in the default configuration. The replacement gate is not papering over the bug — it's a structurally correct meta-gate that was previously enforced implicitly by the buggy `if val_ret > 0.0` check (which happened to also block val=-15 from entering the penalty path, satisfying the C6 contract). The implementer made the implicit contract explicit. The worst-case overfit rule (train=99%, val=-10%) now correctly receives a large penalty when PHASE2_JOINT_TRAIN_VAL=True (the default), which is the production-relevant scenario.
